Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, particularly a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned appearance), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic thromboembolic disease. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal in size, making severe right heart failure less likely than the vascular findings suggest mild to moderate pulmonary hypertension.
